name: PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk

frontmatter.title: CUAN: a Barito-group acquisition vehicle, re-underwritten as a sum of parts
frontmatter.summary: Re-underwritten on the holding-company method card. CUAN's value is the market mark of its stake in the listed contractor Petrosea, plus the group's own coal concessions carried at their reported invested capital and carried value on its projects, less holdco net debt and a holding-company discount. The parts do not carry today's price: SELL, target Rp94, total return -81.5%.
thesis: This name was carried on a commodity-producer template in the first edition. It is not a commodity producer: it is an acquisition vehicle inside the Barito group whose principal asset is a stake in a listed company. The industry classification now says so, and this refresh values it the way the holding-company card requires — a sum of parts with honest marks, not a single-product cash flow.

The sum of the parts is well short of the price. The listed Petrosea stake, the group's own concessions carried at their reported invested capital and the carried value of the projects come to Rp87 a share, and the book cross-check at Rp64 sits below it — the target is set by the parts, not by a single earnings multiple: the P/E leg the first edition carried is struck here, because the only trailing earnings it could capitalise are the non-cash gains below.

The listed mark is a bubble and we say so rather than launder it: Petrosea is capitalised at US$2,182.1m of market value on US$321.4m of its own reported equity and US$1.3m of continuing half-year net profit (a further US$7.6m came from discontinued operations), so marking our stake at market is the single most generous assumption in this note.

Earnings quality remains the hidden problem the first edition identified: audited operating profit is dominated by non-cash investment gains, the group's half-year cash flow from operations is negative after interest and tax, and the finance cost consumes most of a margin the coal ramp has only just restored.

Everything the market pays for beyond the parts sits outside what we can underwrite — the SINI acquisition is still in negotiation with no agreed price, and the new-energy and mineral projects carry no contracted cash flow — so we carry them at cost and flag them in the bull case.

catalysts.event: OJK hands over, in person, the administrative sanction letters from the enforcement round that includes CUAN
Petrosea extraordinary general meeting for the approval of its rights issue, which dilutes the group's listed stake if not taken up
RKAB production-quota approval for FY2027, the supply-discipline lever that governs the group's tonnage plan
FY2026 audited accounts due, the first full year in which the coal ramp and the new offshore EPCI line are both in the base

blocks.text: **This is a refresh, and it changes the method rather than the conclusion.** The first edition valued CUAN on the commodity-producer template: a life-of-asset discounted cash flow of a coal-driven operating book, with an earnings multiple and dividend capacity as cross-checks, and struck a materially lower target on that basis. The industry mapping has since put the name in conglomerates, and the holding-company card governs: listed stakes at market, unlisted parts on their own marks, holdco net debt deducted, and a discount on the whole. On that card the rating is unchanged — **SELL, target Rp94 against a market price of Rp510, a total return of -81.5%** — but the target is higher than the first edition's, because a sum of parts that marks the listed stake at the market's own price is a materially more generous exercise than a coal-only cash flow [S0].

**What the sum of the parts says.** The primary method, weighted 83% of the blend, returns Rp87 a share. It has three components. The first is the group's holding in the listed contractor, Petrosea: 46.7% of its shares at its market capitalisation of US$2,182.1m [S11, S3]. The second is the group's own coal concessions, carried at the group's reported invested capital in the mines — mining properties and stripping activity assets of US$381.9m at the half-year date [S3] — against the company's stated reserves of 228 Mt [S7]. The third is the mineral and power projects, carried at their reported exploration and evaluation value of US$44.3m [S3]. Against those we charge the group's net debt and the holding-company discount [S0]. The earnings cross-check we carried last round is struck this round rather than trimmed: the only trailing earnings it could capitalise are not earnings at all but a non-cash investment gain, so normalised there is no positive base to put a multiple on [S2]. The P/BV cross-check returns Rp64, -26.3% below the primary [S0].

**The most generous assumption in the note is the listed mark.** Petrosea — a mining contractor and engineering group — is capitalised at US$2,182.1m while its own reported equity is US$321.4m and its continuing half-year net profit is US$1.3m [S11, S3]. Marking our stake there is what the card instructs for a listed holding, and a reader who thinks that price is a bubble should read our Rp87 as a ceiling on the parts [S0].

**What moves the value.** The listed mark: it is more than half the gross value of the parts, so Petrosea's price, not the coal price, is the dominant variable [S0]. Then the discount, held at the middle of the house band (30%) and the channel the scenarios widen to reach that mark; then the financing — a discount rate of 10.7% charged on the whole against an EBITDA the half year only begins to cover [S3, S0].

PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) is an energy and resources group assembled by acquisition inside the Barito group, with Prajogo Pangestu's interests holding the great majority of the shares (82.2% of the register is insider-held) and a free float of 19.5% [S2, S0]. The structure is a holding one in substance: the parent holds operating subsidiaries directly and a listed company through a wholly owned vehicle, and the single most valuable entry on this note's balance sheet is that listed stake [S3].

The group reports three segments. Mining covers both the group's own coal sales and the mining contracting it performs for others; engineering and construction and the offshore EPCI line are the contracting businesses; services is the logistics and port arm [S3]. The revenue note splits the half-year total of US$736.1m into coal sales of US$249.3m, mining services, construction and engineering, services and the new offshore oil-and-gas EPCI line, in roughly equal thirds between coal and the contracting complex [S3]. That split matters: the cash the group earns from its own concessions is a minority of consolidated revenue, and the contracting lines are pass-through work with a thin margin and concentrated counterparties [S3].

The listed subsidiary is Petrosea, in which the group holds 46.7% and which it consolidates because it also holds a control statement from another shareholder [S3]. Petrosea brings the mining contracting, the engineering and construction business, the new offshore EPCI line, and — through the Hafar, HBS and Scan-Bilt acquisitions — contracting in Papua New Guinea [S2, S3]. It earned US$543.5m of revenue and US$1.3m of continuing net profit in the half year, on equity of US$321.4m — to which the same note adds a discontinued-operation profit of US$7.6m that the interim filing labels but does not name, sitting in the mining segment and already inside Petrosea's traded price [S3].

The group's own coal business runs through named subsidiaries with disclosed licences and lives: Multi Tambangjaya Utama holds a generation-three coal contract of work with the longest tenure, alongside Tamtama Perkasa, Borneo Bangun Banua, Intan Bumi Persada, Cristian Eka Pratama and the two development concessions [S2, S7]. Gold and silver sit in Intam, silica sand in Silika Salut Jaya, and the power project in the Guna Darma Integra vehicle [S7]. The growth strategy is acquisition-led: the company has begun negotiations to acquire control of PT Singaraja Putra, which has not closed [S2].

The footprint is domestic — Central and East Kalimantan — with the Papua New Guinea and offshore arms coming through the listed subsidiary [S2]. Competitively the group is a challenger in coal, and its integration — hauling, barging, port and contracting — is a real cost advantage; the related-party web that funds it is the channel the earnings-quality card tells us to scrutinise [S2, S3].

The industry frame for this name is a conglomerate frame, not a coal frame, and that is the change this refresh makes. The group's cash generation is driven by thermal and metallurgical coal, which is supply-disciplined and policy-rationed in Indonesia: production is gated by the annual RKAB work plan and budget, and the domestic market obligation requires producers to sell a share of output into a capped domestic power market [S2, S7]. The company names compliance with the domestic obligation as a risk in its own annual report, and states the royalty rate it pays on open-pit coal at or above 5,200 kcal/kg as 13.5% [S2, F14].

The macro desk's regime is balance-of-payments pressure, neutral on thermal coal and averse on the rate-sensitive, current-account-levered domestic complex [S0]. That matters twice: the group is a leveraged domestic vehicle with a dollar-reporting balance sheet and rupiah-denominated debt, so the exchange rate of Rp18,350/USD is a live translation risk on debt serviced from dollar cash flow [S0, S3]; and the coal price is the driver our own deck carries, so the deck's path — not the company's ambition — is the revenue ceiling [S0].

The relevant peer set is the conglomerate and holding-company group on this desk, not the coal producers: a thermal producer is valued on reserve life and cash margin, while a holding company is valued on the market marks of what it holds, less its own costs and debt, and then discounted because that is what holding companies trade at [S0]. Market structure in the group's own markets is unfavourable to pricing power: mining contracting is competitive, the group is a mid-tier coal producer with no first-quartile cost claim, and the buyers are concentrated [S3]. The moat, such as it is, is the licence base and the logistics corridor, and section four marks it at the invested capital the group carries [S7, S3].

Consolidated revenue reached US$1,215.6m in FY2025 on coal sales of US$423.4m and the contracting book, and the half year to June 2026 ran at US$736.1m, up by roughly three-fifths on the comparable half of the prior year [S2, S3]. Our forecast holds the half-year's revenue run rate into the full year and tapers thereafter, and the margin structure at the half-year's own level: gross margin of 13.8%, an opex charge of 5.7% of revenue and depreciation, depletion and amortisation of 12.7% [S3]. That gives an EBITDA margin of roughly a fifth and an operating line that finally clears the interest charge, unlike the last audited year [S3].

The last audited year is the reason this note opens with the earnings-quality card. FY2025's reported operating profit was US$239.1m, of which US$193.7m was other operating income that the company describes as investment gains on other financial assets — non-cash, and most of the total [S2]. Strip it out and the group's audited operating profit was a fraction of its gross profit of US$160.0m; the engine's EBIT line, excluding that income, is US$25.3m [S2, S0]. The cash-flow statement tells the same story from the other side: after interest and tax payments the group used US$-27.6m of cash in operating activities in FY2025, a year for which it reported net profit of US$152.0m [S2]. The half year is better but not clean: operating cash flow before interest and tax was positive, and after finance costs and tax it was still a use of cash, while finance expenses of US$57.5m ran against gross profit of US$101.6m [S3].

Restating the data pack from the filing remains part of this refresh. The pack's depreciation is a small fraction of the audited charge, its dividend paid is several times the distribution the accounts show, and its interest expense is below the filing's finance line [S0, S2]. Each is an optics-class item, disclosed rather than concealed, not a manipulation-class flag [S2]. The depreciation restatement now runs history and forecast on one footing: the last audited year's charge is the full group figure of US$155.3m from the operating-segment note, not the cost-of-revenue depreciation component alone, so the audited year's clean EBITDA of US$180.6m and the forecast D&A rate are measured the same way and the year-on-year margin comparison is not distorted by a change of base [S2].

The balance sheet is where the holding-company frame bites. At the FY2025 balance-sheet date the group carried interest-bearing debt of US$1,448.7m [S0]; at the half-year date the filing shows short-term bank loans of US$63.2m inside a debt stack that also runs to long-term bank lines, bonds and sukuk, against cash of US$220.2m and further financial assets of US$228.8m [S3]. The data pack strikes the half-year debt at its own total [S0], and our model rolls the cash forward to US$349.3m by the end of FY2026E — a forecast, not an actual. Parent equity was US$347.2m and the non-controlling interest US$271.0m, almost all of which sits in the listed subsidiary [S3]. Capital spending ran at US$72.9m in the half year, funded by the shelf bond and sukuk programme — US$178.8m of target proceeds across two phases — and by bank facilities in which the listed subsidiary and the parent are joint borrowers [S3]. The dividend is a token: US$2.0m, or US$0.0002 a share [S2].

The method set is the industry default for conglomerates and it is the right one here. The group's most valuable asset is a holding in another listed company, and no single-product cash-flow model can carry that: a coal template would either ignore the holding or double-count the contracting revenue that flows through it [S3]. A sum of the parts treats each claim separately. The cost of capital is built on the dollar risk-free rate of 5.0%, the industry unlevered beta of 0.90 re-levered to the group's debt-to-equity of 0.45 to give 1.22, and a mature-market equity risk premium plus a country premium, for a cost of equity of 13.1% and a weighted average cost of capital of 10.7% [S0]. No liquidity discount applies: the shares trade 357,641,686,695.2 a day [S0].

The primary method is the sum of the parts, weighted 83% of the blend. Its first component is the listed stake: 46.7% of Petrosea at its market capitalisation of US$2,182.1m, a market mark taken on the day Petrosea disclosed its rights issue and the single largest entry in the note [S11, S3]. The second is the group's own coal concessions, carried at the group's reported invested capital in the mines — mining properties and stripping activity assets of US$381.9m at the half-year date [S3] — against the company's stated reserves of 228 Mt [S7]. Those mining properties are the group's own coal-concession areas of interest, the Tamtama Perkasa and MUTU holdings, and the group's mining permits and contract of work are held by the coal subsidiaries, not by the listed contract-mining subsidiary, so the block is not double-counted against the Petrosea mark we carry above [S3]. We carry it at book rather than on a multiple, for a stated reason: the company prints no segment EBITDA, and its only printed EBITDA figure is the one the first edition showed to be dominated by non-cash investment gains, so a multiple of it would import the earnings-quality problem [S4, S2], while a value per reserve tonne would need a transaction or peer benchmark the archives do not carry. The third is the projects, at the reported exploration and evaluation carrying value of US$44.3m, which is the floor the most-likely card requires for development assets rather than an estimate of their worth [S3]. One item we do not add as a fourth component, and say so: the equity-method investment in associates of US$34.0m [S3] is not marked separately, because its material financial-services leg is held through the listed subsidiary's own subsidiary and so already sits inside the Petrosea market mark, and the residual is immaterial against the parts — marking it would double-count the mark [S3]. From the sum we deduct holdco net debt struck at the group level less the listed subsidiary's debt taken by entity, because that debt is already inside the market mark of the stake, and then apply the holding-company discount [S3]. The deduction is itemised rather than asserted: the three Petrosea legs named by entity in the filing are its share of the syndicated facilities (US$161.9m, [S3]), its own bond programme of US$53.4m plus US$56.0m [S3], and its own sukuk ijarah of US$26.2m plus US$28.0m [S3], while the parent's own programmes — bonds of US$112.0m and sukuk wakalah of US$19.6m plus US$36.4m — and the entity-unattributed bank lines stay in the charge, the latter the conservative direction for a SELL [S3]. The engine carries the listed stake on its book-value path because Petrosea has no coverage packet of its own; the input is the market capitalisation, not a book value, and we flag the label so a reader is not misled [S0].

The discount is the base rate, not the opportunity. House practice is that holding-company discounts persist indefinitely, and the question is not whether CUAN trades below its parts but whether a named, dated catalyst will close the gap. We hold the discount at the middle of the house band, 30%: there is no holdco-level buyback or tender, no asset sale or subsidiary listing, and no change in upstreaming policy — the Petrosea rights issue is a capital call on the group, not a distribution to it [S9, S11]. The name's own five-year discount history cannot be computed (it listed in 2023; no entity-level sum-of-the-parts series exists in the data we hold), so the house base rate is the only anchor and we say so [S0]. We sit above the bottom of the band because the governance file argues for a wider discount, and short of the wide end because the sanction attaches to a listing participant rather than the company and the round's licence-freeze is another issuer's underwriter licence [S8]. The FY2026 audit at the end of April 2027 is the monitor we set [S2].

Look-through, the numbers the consolidated accounts hide are worth stating. The group's 46.7% stake in Petrosea earned US$543.5m of revenue and US$1.3m of continuing profit in the half year, on Petrosea's own equity of US$321.4m, and the subsidiary's borrowings sit inside the consolidated debt we deduct [S3]. Upstreaming — the card's single quality metric — is thin: the only distribution in the record is a parent token of US$2.0m, with no subsidiary dividend large enough to fund the holdco and no stated upstream policy, so the parent's claim on the subsidiary's cash is a control right rather than a demonstrated flow [S2, S3].

The earnings cross-check is struck, and that is the method change this round makes. Last round the blend carried a P/E leg at a load-bearing weight; it capitalised the last audited year's parent profit, which is not earnings but a non-cash investment gain — the group's profit before tax of US$149.3m is smaller than its other operating income of US$193.7m, so on a normalised basis the group was loss-making on operations in its last audited year [S2]. Capitalising that at a peer multiple was unsupported optimism in a load-bearing number, and we have removed the leg rather than keep it at a token weight: a multiple applied to a contaminated metric is not a cross-check. The method set is therefore the primary plus a single cross-check rather than the usual three — with the earnings leg struck there is no clean second cross-check to add, and an honest two-leg set beats a three-leg one that leans on a contaminated metric. The P/BV method remains as that cross-check. It applies 1.1 to parent book and lands -26.3% below the primary, because that book of US$347.2m is a thin equity after a heavily leveraged build and a book method cannot see the listed stake at more than its carrying value [S0, S3]. The target is therefore set by the parts, and the surviving cross-check sits below them because the parts mark the listed stake where the market does and the mines at their reported invested capital [S0].

What does the price imply? Run the primary method backwards and today's price is not consistent with any discount inside the house band: the blended value before discount, carried forward at the cost of equity, is Rp83 a share, and even a zero holding-company discount leaves the parts far below the traded price [S0]. The engine reports no bracketing solution for the reverse discount, which is the finding: the market is not applying a discount to these parts, it is pricing something not in them [S0]. The plausible candidate is the platform story — a controlling shareholder, a listed contractor priced at many times its book, an acquisition pipeline with a named target still in negotiation, and a new-energy portfolio with no contracted cash flow [S2, S11, S7]. We can say the parts we can source do not support the price; we cannot say what does, and we do not invent it [S0].

The sensitivity grid runs the holding-company discount against the cost of equity, because those are now the two variables that move this valuation [S0]. It is compressed at the top: a narrower discount helps, but cannot bridge the gap to the traded price on its own, because the parts are the constraint — a holdco's target is set by what it holds.

**The listed mark is now the dominant risk, in both directions.** More than half the gross value of the parts is a stake in Petrosea marked at its traded price, and that price is capitalised at many times Petrosea's own book and earnings [S11, S3]. Petrosea's shares fell sharply on the rights-issue news [F53] and were volatile enough that the exchange wrote to the company about it; the company replied that it had withheld no material fact, while acknowledging it was aware of the news about MSCI's evaluation of the Indonesian market — an index event, not a company one, but one that can carry the mark without any change in the business [S10]. The rights issue dilutes a holder that does not subscribe by up to 1.7%, is capped at 1.7% of Petrosea's capital, and leaves the parent a choice between laying out cash for its 46.7% share and accepting the dilution [S9]; the subscription price is not yet disclosed, so we size it as a claim on the group's US$220.2m of cash rather than a fixed number [S9, S3]. A de-rating of the listed subsidiary is felt twice: once in the mark, and once in the sentiment that carries the parent [S10].

**The discount can widen while you wait.** The house base rate is that these discounts persist and no catalyst to narrow this one is present; the group's dividend is a token (US$2.0m in FY2025), so there is no cash return while you wait [S2]. That carry risk is what makes a wide discount on its own an insufficient thesis.

**Governance and regulatory risk.** The regulator's enforcement round names CUAN alongside two other Barito-linked issuers, with a sanction falling on a subscriber over concealed orders in CUAN's own listing [S8]. The round's licence-freeze headline is an underwriter's licence in another issuer's case, and the further participant sanctions fall on exchange members, not on CUAN or its mining licences — we checked the scope and it touches no licence of this group [S8]. Related-party revenue was US$34.6m in the half year [S3]. Neither is a manipulation-class finding — both are disclosed — but both widen the warranted discount, which is why we sit above the bottom of the band [S8, S3].

**Financing and liquidity risk.** Net debt is large against an EBITDA the half year only just covers after interest, finance expense was US$57.5m in a single half year against gross profit of US$101.6m, and the model does not repay debt [S3, S0]. The capital programme has been funded with bank facilities and two phases of a shelf bond and sukuk programme, so any interruption to capital access is a direct risk to the ramp [S3, F56].

**Execution risk.** The SINI acquisition remains in negotiation with no agreed price or timetable [S2]; we exclude it from the base case, though the larger reserve figure the company projects depends on it.

The scenarios shock two inputs, mirrored in both directions: the holding-company discount, widened to the extremes the engine admits, and the cost of equity [S0]. The listed mark is a static sourced mark the engine does not itself shock; since it is more than half the gross value, the discount is the channel that reaches it, and we say so rather than imply a test we cannot run [S0]. The revenue-path shock the first edition carried is dropped, not kept: the parts are static marks, so a revenue shock moved no valuation input at all and bought false width. The spread the two live shocks produce is real rather than cosmetic, because it moves the mark through the discount. The bear case pushes the discount past the top of the house band, lifts the cost of equity, and reads as a de-rating of the mark towards Petrosea's own reported equity as the absence of a narrowing catalyst bites; the bull is the market being right: the discount narrows below the bottom of the band on a completed rights issue and a closed acquisition, and the mark is sustained [S9, S2]. Even the bull leaves the parts short of the traded price: what would move the rating from above is a mark we can source (a priced SINI deal, a crystallised stake value or a Petrosea price we can defend), not a narrower discount. Signposts that would change the view are a holdco-level capital return; a priced SINI transaction; a stake increase or disposal that crystallises a mark; and the FY2026 audited accounts [S2, S3].

Control sits with Prajogo Pangestu's Barito interests — insider holdings are 82.2% against a free float of 19.5% — so minority holders are price-takers in every structural decision [S0]. The company was assembled by acquisition, and its most valuable asset is a listed company it controls through its own shares and a third party's control statement, a structure that concentrates decision-making further [S3].

The regulatory file is the most material governance item and it is dated. In October 2026 the capital markets regulator handed over administrative sanction letters from an enforcement round that includes CUAN alongside two other issuers in the same group, with a fine of IDR100.0bn on a subscriber that concealed its share-order information in CUAN's own public offering and a larger fine on a subscriber over another issuer's listing [S8]. The sanction attaches to a listing participant rather than the company, but it is a governance-discount input, not a footnote. The scope is precise: the round's licence-freeze is an underwriter's licence in the DSSA case and the further participant sanctions fall on exchange members and market participants — none on CUAN or its mining licences [S8]. It is the single most recent dated event in this name [S8].

Related-party dealings are a structural feature rather than an exception: consolidated revenue from related parties was US$34.6m in the half year, and the group's facilities have the parent as a joint borrower with the operating subsidiaries [S3]. Pledged-share disclosure and auditor changes are not flagged in the material the company has published in this cycle; we record that as an absence of evidence rather than a clean bill of health [S2]. On dividends the record is thin: a token distribution of US$2.0m, approved in April and paid in May 2025, with no interim policy since [S2]. On ESG the group discloses a mine reclamation and closure provision, and the larger exposure is the domestic-market obligation together with the permitting footprint of a rapidly acquired licence base [S2, S3].

The dated catalysts are in the frontmatter: the regulator's sanction letters, already delivered; the listed subsidiary's general meeting on its rights issue, which we watch for the take-up and the price; the FY2027 work-plan approval, which sets the tonnage ceiling; and the FY2026 audit [S8, S9, S7, S2].

Between updates we monitor four things. The listed subsidiary's traded price, because it is more than half the gross value of the parts [S11]. The group's mines' reported invested capital and licence status, because the coal mark is a carrying value that moves with the concession base and its depletion [S3, S7]. The half-year margin and the cash conversion, because the last audited year's profit was mostly non-cash [S3, S2]. And the financing: the debt maturity ladder and any new facility, because the model does not repay debt and the finance charge consumes most of the operating margin [S3].

suspended.reason: Rating withdrawn while the name is re-run under the V5.2 konglo lens (group and HSC context, regime-based most-likely target); the new report replaces it.

base.narrative: The parts as they stand: the listed Petrosea stake at its 15 October 2026 market mark, the group's own mines at their reported invested capital, the exploration portfolio at its carrying value, group net debt less the listed subsidiary's debt taken by entity, and a 30% holding-company discount with no narrowing catalyst yet dated.

bear.narrative: The listed mark is the swing factor and it gives back: Petrosea de-rates from a capitalisation of many times its own book and continuing earnings towards something nearer its own reported equity, and the parent's 46.71% stake is worth proportionally less. The discount is the channel that carries that de-rating into the target — it widens PAST the top of the 20-40% house band as the OJK file stays open and the 23 November rights issue is taken up only partially, diluting the stake without bringing cash to the holdco — and the higher cost of equity the balance-of-payments regime implies is charged on the whole. Coal demand discipline keeps the group's own tonnage at the plan rather than above it. The SINI acquisition does not close, so the group's projected reserve base stays at the 228.29 Mt already on the books.

bull.narrative: The market is right and we are wrong on the mark: Petrosea's price is sustained or re-rated further as the rights issue funds its engineering and construction book, the parent takes up its share and keeps its 46.71% whole, the SINI acquisition closes and adds reserves to the concessions already marked, and the group's 30 Mt/yr ambition is delivered. A holdco-level catalyst then crystallises the discount towards the narrow end of the band — a higher upstream dividend, a sub-level capital return or a stake sale at a mark — and the cost of equity falls as the balance-of-payments pressure eases.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 24%, below the half year's own pace: 1H2026 consolidated revenue of US$736.105m was up 59% on the comparable half of 2025 (S3), so a full year at that run rate would be far above the FY2025A base of US$1,215.618m; 24% is the taper towards the long-run coal-ramp pace as the group plan of >30 Mt/yr by 2031 (F13) and the >US$1bn order book are absorbed. No decline is assumed: costs and volumes follow the last actual.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Held at the 1H2026 LK margin: gross profit US$101.627m on revenue US$736.105m (S3) = 13.8%. The FY2023-25 average (22.0%) is distorted by the pre-acquisition FY2023 base and is not the current economics; the method card says costs stay at the last actual in real terms.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Stripped of the half-year's other operating income, which the red team correctly says we must not capitalise. 1H2026 gross profit US$101.627m less operating profit US$68.499m gives a cost block of US$33.128m on revenue US$736.105m, but that operating profit already carries other operating income of +US$9.060m (S3 note 40, part-quoted F68), so the ex-other-income cost is US$42.188m = 5.73% of revenue. The half-year's other income is not recurring: it is a US$42.717m FX gain (F69) net of a US$13.149m credit-loss allowance (F71) and a US$14.352m fair-value loss on the FVTPL portfolio (F70), the same non-cash mix the report condemns in FY2025A. This line also carries the final tax the LK charges above operating profit (US$4.847m, F72), which is why the forecast tax rate below is not the group's combined tax burden.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the 1H2026 LK depreciation, depletion and amortisation of US$93.619m on revenue US$736.105m (S3) = 12.7% — the FY2023-25 default (5.9%) understates a group whose mining properties and stripping assets are now US$381.867m (S3). This half-year figure is the full charge (all three elements), and it is the honest full-year rate. History is now keyed on the SAME basis: the FY2025A da fact (F82) is the full group charge of US$155.318m from the operating-segment note (S2), not the cost-of-revenue depreciation component alone, so the FY+1 forecast rate and the last actual year are measured on one footing.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the 1H2026 run rate: acquisitions of property, plant and equipment of US$72.901m on revenue US$736.105m (S3), i.e. 9.9% annualised. The FY2024-25 default (21.9%) is an acquisition-era number and is not a maintenance spend.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Reverted from the engine default to the last-actual balance sheet. The FY2023-25 average (34.09%) is an artefact of the pre-acquisition FY2023 base, when the group carried almost no working capital; the last balance sheet (30 June 2026, S0 latest_bs) carries working capital of US$278.437m against an annualised revenue base of US$1,472.210m, i.e. 18.91%. Holding that ratio is the most-likely reading: the coal ramp and the new offshore EPCI line both build receivables and contract assets, and no source shows the ratio falling.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Set from the LK's own arithmetic rather than asserted: the half-year income tax charge below profit before tax is US$5.443m (F73, note 25) on profit before tax of US$14.287m (S3) = 38.1%. The earlier 10% note was wrong — it was neither the statutory rate nor the effective one. The final tax regime is already a cost in the opex line above (US$4.847m in the half year, F72, charged above operating profit), so this rate is the below-the-line charge only and the two do not double-count. The rate is high because the half-year pre-tax base is thin: operating profit of US$68.499m carries US$57.513m of finance expense.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Blended coupon on the reported debt: 1H2026 finance expenses of US$57.513m annualised on opening debt of US$1,448.749m (S3) implies ~8%, and the group's public bonds and sukuk carry 6.75-9.00% coupons (S3); set at 8.5%.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Held at the 1H2026 run rate: finance income of US$3.301m annualised over opening cash of US$453.801m (S3) = ~1.5%.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: the group funded itself in 1H2026 with net new bank loans of US$59.6m but repaid as much as it drew (S3), and no sourced refinancing plan exists at the parent beyond the Petrosea rights issue, which is at the subsidiary.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Set to the non-controlling interests' share of group equity at 30 June 2026, 291.210 / (347.161 + 291.210) = 45.62% (F67 and F54, S3), because the profit-attribution routes do not produce a forward rate. The 1H2026 attribution is parent US$19.780m against non-controlling interests of MINUS US$3.316m (F58, F59, S3 p.8) — a negative minority share driven by the US$7.620m discontinued profit (F57) that accrues to Petrosea's 53.29% minority (F66) and by loss-making continuing operations at Equator Sumber Energi; capitalising either number would flatter parent earnings in a way no source supports. The FY2023-25 average (4.81%) cannot represent the forward group either: it is dominated by the pre-acquisition FY2023 base, when the group was one small coal miner, while 53.29% of Petrosea and 35.00% of Equator Sumber Energi now sit outside the parent. The equity proportion is the reproducible structural anchor.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Held at ~2% of parent earnings: the FY2025 AGMS approved a cash dividend of US$2.000m, or US$0.00017791 a share (S2/F29-F30), which is ~1.5% of FY2025 parent profit; the group is a capital-hungry acquisition vehicle, not a dividend payer.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: 112,418,900,000 shares after the 1:10 stock split (S2/F31); the Petrosea rights issue is at the subsidiary, not the parent (S9/S11), and such parent-level issue as it implies (a maximum 1.66% dilution of the listed stake, F75) is carried as a risk, not as a parent share change.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for the reporting currency: the group reports in US dollars (S3) so the dollar cap of 2.5% applies and the long-run rate is held at the 2.0% house default rather than at the group's own growth, which is an acquisition artefact and not a terminal rate.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Held at 30%, the middle of the 20-40% house band, and the choice is argued rather than asserted. The name's own five-year discount history cannot be computed — the group listed in 2023 and no entity-level SOTP series exists in the data we hold (S0 own_history is empty) — so the house base rate for holdcos, that 20-40% persists indefinitely by default, is the only anchor available; we say so rather than implying an own-history check we could not run. We widen from the bottom of the band to 30% for the governance file: the OJK enforcement round names CUAN alongside DSSA and BREN, with a Rp100bn fine on a subscriber that concealed its order book in CUAN's own listing (S8/F36), and the further participant sanctions in the same round attach to the CUAN case (F77). We do not go to the wide end for a stated reason: the sanction is on a listing participant, not on the company, the licence-freeze in the round is an underwriter's licence in the DSSA case and touches no mining licence of this group (F76), and the PTRO mark is already carried at the market's own generous price, so a top-of-band discount would double-count caution. A dated narrowing catalyst exists and is tracked: Petrosea's RUPSLB on 23 November 2026 for the rights issue (S9, S11) — a capital call on the group, not a distribution to it, which is why the discount is not narrowed now. The scenario tails deliberately run past the band (bear 45%, bull 15%): the discount is the only channel the scenario layer has into a static listed mark, so the tails test whether the mark de-rating the report calls for can move the target, and a symmetric +/-0.15 is the widest shock the engine admits (S0).

challenges.challenge: The coal block is US$684.87m = 228.29 Mt (F33) x a multiple of 3.0, i.e. an asserted US$3.00 per tonne of in-ground reserves — 39% of gross SOTP. No archived source quotes or supports US$3.0/t: S7 (p.17) gives tonnage only, no margin, cost, royalty, calorific or licence-life calibration, and no comparable transaction is cited. The stated design was a multiple on sourced segment EBITDA or book, and the company prints no segment EBITDA, so this is a typed number, not a sourced mark.
challenges.answer: Re-marked on the book-value basis the challenge offers. The coal block is now the group reported invested capital in the mines — mining properties and stripping activity assets of US$381.867m at 30 June 2026 (F45, quote Properti pertambangan dan aset aktivitas pengupasan lapisan tanah ... 381.867, S3 p.5). The typed US$3.00/t reserve multiple is deleted; the report carries the mines at that carrying value against the stated reserves (F33) rather than pricing reserves per tonne, and states that no transaction benchmark exists rather than inventing one.

challenges.challenge: holdco_net_debt is hardcoded at US$641.0 with no fact id and a note that cannot be reproduced: group net debt US$1,426.519m less US$449.092m (S0/S3) = US$977.4m, 'less Petrosea's own borrowing' — but no PTRO debt total or PTRO cash figure is fact-keyed. The note nets PTRO's debt out of the mark while leaving PTRO's cash inside the netted US$449.092m (which is exactly 220.245 cash + 228.847 other financial assets), and the identifiable PTRO borrowings alone (short-term 63.228 + syndicated share 161.862 + its bonds 109.375 = ~334.5) sit inside an unitemised residual. The reader cannot verify US$641.0.
challenges.answer: Rebuilt as an itemised, fact-keyed schedule. Group debt US$1,426.519m at 30 June 2026 = short-term bank loans F63 63.228, current bonds 6.607, sukuk F81 3.523, bank loans 127.121, leases 11.063, non-current bonds 213.639, sukuk F64 106.069, bank loans 877.207, leases 18.062 (S3 balance sheet). Cash US$449.092m = cash F61 220.245 plus other financial assets F62 228.847 (FVTPL instruments, not demand deposits). The PTRO legs are excluded by name — syndicated share F51 161.862 and sukuk ijarah 109.592 (F64+F81) — giving holdco net debt US$705.973m. Two limits are stated rather than hidden: residual parent bank lines stay in (conservative for a SELL) and the PTRO own cash is not disclosed separately so it stays inside the cash line (generous).

challenges.challenge: opex_pct 4.5% is 'net of' 1H2026 other operating income of +US$9.060m (fund record lines 45-48), which the LK decomposes into a +US$42.717m FX gain, -US$13.149m credit-loss allowance and -US$14.352m loss on other financial assets (S3 note 40). The base case therefore capitalises volatile FX gains and paper marks into every forecast year (~US$18.6m/yr of FY2026E EBIT), the same earnings-quality flaw the report condemns in FY2025A.
challenges.answer: opex_pct stripped to the ex-other-income run rate. Gross profit US$101.627m less operating profit US$68.499m = US$33.128m; adding back other operating income US$9.060m (F68) gives US$42.188m = 5.73% of revenue, held flat, replacing the 4.5% that capitalised the gain. F69 FX gain 42.717, F71 credit-loss 13.149 and F70 FVTPL loss 14.352 are named as non-recurring, and the final tax (F72 4.847) carried in this line is flagged so the below-the-line tax rate does not double-count. The calibration justification is restated accordingly.

challenges.challenge: tax_rate is set at 10% with a basis citing 1H2026 tax expense US$5.443m on PBT US$14.287m (S3) — a ratio of 38.1%, not 10%. The engine then also charges final tax (US$4.847m in 1H26) above the line inside opex, so the 10% rate double-counts the final-tax regime's leniency and overstates forecast net profit and EPS every year.
challenges.answer: tax_rate set from the LK arithmetic: 1H2026 income tax expense US$5.443m (F73, note 25) on profit before tax US$14.287m = 38.1%, charged below the line only. The final tax US$4.847m (F72) is already a cost inside opex, so the two do not double-count and the 10% note is withdrawn.

challenges.challenge: minority_pct 4.8124% is the FY2023-25 average, but 1H2026 attribution is parent US$19.780m vs NCI -US$3.316m on net profit US$16.464m (S3 p.8), and the note admits the balance 'includes the discontinued Petrosea leg' without splitting it. With NCI equity at US$291.210m (45.6% of total equity), the forecast structurally over-attributes earnings to the parent in every year.
challenges.answer: minority_pct moved off the FY2023-25 average to the structural equity proportion at 30 June 2026: non-controlling interest US$291.210m (F67) over total equity US$638.371m = 45.62%. The basis explains that neither the FY2023-25 average (a pre-acquisition artefact) nor the 1H2026 attribution (parent US$19.780m vs NCI -US$3.316m, F58/F59, distorted by the discontinued leg F57) is a forward rate, and the equity proportion is the reproducible structural anchor.

challenges.challenge: The 'bubble' argument prices PTRO on half-year net profit of US$1.313m (F49), but PTRO's summarised P&L in the same note shows a further US$7.620m profit from discontinued operations (S3 NCI note, p.186), i.e. total PTRO net profit of US$8.933m — 6.8x the quoted figure. The discontinued operation is never identified, and no held-for-sale asset, divestment proceed or contingent consideration appears in valuation.bridge although the most-likely card requires post-balance-sheet and held-for-sale items to be valued.
challenges.answer: F49 relabelled continuing-only and its label now names F57 as the discontinued leg, so the Petrosea total 1H2026 net profit is the sum of the two; the report gives both. The interim filing labels the discontinued operation but does not name it; it sits in the Mining segment column of the segment note (S3 p.186, p.204). It is a realised pre-balance-sheet item already inside the Petrosea traded price, so no bridge value is booked and the reason is stated in valuation.post_bs_review rather than left implicit.

challenges.challenge: F33 reserves (228.29 Mt) are stated as at December 2024, 22 months stale at the report date, include IBP's 12.5 Mt on 'internal analysis' (S7 p.17), and are pre-SINI — while the bull case simultaneously assumes the SINI acquisition closes and adds reserves, and the >30 Mt/yr 2031 ambition (F13) depends on that same unclosed deal. The SINI-contingent 378 Mt projection (F5) is press-sourced, not filed.
challenges.answer: The F33 label now date-stamps the reserve statement, flags that the Intan Bumi Persada tonnage carries the source own internal-analysis asterisk, and states that it predates the unclosed SINI acquisition. The SINI-contingent 378 Mt (F5, press-sourced) is excluded from the base mark and from the bear, and the bull narrative names SINI as the contingency that adds reserves only if it closes, so the base and bull treatment are consistent.

challenges.challenge: Both scenarios shock only the holdco discount (+/-10pp) and revenue growth (+/-3pp) — but revenue growth has no channel into the SOTP target (holdings rows are static marks), and the listed PTRO mark, called 'the dominant risk, in both directions', is never shocked although both narratives centre on it. The mirrored shocks produce a symmetric 137-161 grid in which no probability-weighted path tests the market being right (sustained PTRO mark, closed SINI, platform value), so the -71% call is never stress-tested from above.
challenges.answer: The scenarios now shock three inputs, not two: holding-company discount, cost of equity and revenue-growth, mirrored in both directions. The engine scenario layer cannot target a holdings row or valuation.bridge, so a direct PTRO-mark shock is impossible; qc_justifications scenario.ptro_mark states this and the discount (the mark is more than half gross value) is the proportionate channel that reaches the mark. The bear and bull narratives name the mark de-rating to near book and its sustained re-rating, and section 5 adds the market-right signposts.

challenges.challenge: The 30% discount is set at the middle of the house band with 'no named, dated catalyst' identified, no own-5y discount range (the method card's required anchor), no catalyst_date in frontmatter, and no look-through earnings, look-through leverage, upstream dividend coverage ratio or factor tags. The text argues the governance file supports 'the wide end of the band' (section 4) yet selects the middle without bridging the gap — and at a market price 3.4x the pre-discount SOTP, the discount framing itself is unanchored.
challenges.answer: Added the own-five-year statement (uncomputable — listed 2023, no entity-level sum-of-the-parts series, S0 own_history empty) with what it implies; a dated monitor (FY2026 audit, catalyst_date 2027-04-30) plus the 23 November 2026 rights meeting; look-through revenue, profit and equity of the Petrosea stake and the thin upstream coverage (only a token parent dividend F29, no disclosed subsidiary upstream policy); and a one-line 30%-vs-40% justification tied to the OJK file scope (F76/F77 — the sanction hits a listing participant, not the company).

challenges.challenge: The SOTP bridge omits three required or evident items: (i) no holdco opex capitalised at ~10x as the method card instructs; (ii) non-PTRO minorities (ESE US$18.104m + Volta US$2.096m, S3 p.184) are never deducted although the coal/projects marks are pre-minority; (iii) the US$44.332m 'development projects' row claims to cover the 680 MW GDI power project but its only evidence is the exploration-and-evaluation asset line, with no quote tying GDI's carrying value to that line.
challenges.answer: The bridge now deducts the non-Petrosea minorities (Equator Sumber Energi F65 18.104 plus Volta Energi Nusantara F80 2.096 = US$20.2m) because the coal and project marks are carried before minorities; the Petrosea own 53.29% minority is not deducted (it sits outside the market mark). GDI is excluded from holdings with a stated reason — the LK gives no carrying value tying the 680 MW project to the exploration line — and flagged as unsourced upside. The holdco-opex at about 10x is answered in qc_justifications valuation.holdco_opex: no parent-only cost base is disclosed, so it cannot be sized from a source.

challenges.challenge: The P/E cross-check claims to apply 'the name's own-history multiple' (fund record line 239) but the engine used peer median 8.73x ('own history unavailable'), applied to FY2025A parent earnings of US$134.567m that the note itself shows were dominated by US$193.701m of non-cash other operating income — then weighted 25% of the target (+US$47.4 of the US$149.25 target) while the text says 'we do not lean on it'.
challenges.answer: The report now calls the multiple peer-median (the engine basis is peer median, own history unavailable) and states the 2023 listing as why no own-history series exists; the weight is cut to 10% of the blend with the reason stated in the text and in qc_justifications.weights.changed. The metric it capitalises is FY2025A parent earnings dominated by US$193.701m of non-cash other operating income (F20), which is why the weight is cut rather than the metric cleaned.

challenges.challenge: Two history inputs embed unsourced drift in opposite directions: (a) the D&A restatement keys only F6/F7 fixed-asset depreciation (US$106.099m) while F8/F9 depletion (US$29.924m) and amortisation (US$16.089m) sit keyless, so FY2025A EBITDA prints US$131.423m instead of ~US$177.4m — the extreme_call justification then cites the understated figure against US$977.4m net debt (7.6x vs ~5.5x leverage); (b) nwc_pct 34.09% jumps FY2026E working capital to US$513.9m from US$156.5m actual (a US$357.4m FY2026E cash drain, collapsing model cash to US$138.7m) on an 'engine default' basis with the 1H26-consistency claim uncited.
challenges.answer: The engine restatement takes one filing figure per period (facts_index is last-wins on key+period), so the da fact carries fixed-asset depreciation F6 106.099 alone; keying F8/F9 as da would overwrite it, not sum. The full charge F6+F8+F9 = US$152.112m and the approximately US$177.4m EBITDA the challenge computes are stated in the report and in qc_justifications extreme_call and calibration, and the leverage framing is corrected off the understated figure. nwc_pct reverted from the 34.09% default to the last-actual 18.91% (working capital US$278.437m over annualised revenue US$1,472.210m, S0 latest_bs/S3).

challenges.challenge: The balance-sheet paragraph mislabels its own figures: 'interest-bearing debt of {{fin.FY2025A.debt}}' (US$1,448.749m, the FY2025A year-end) is presented as the half-year position (actual 30 Jun 2026: US$1,426.519m per market data), and cash is given as the model's FY2026E roll (US$138.7m) rather than the LK actuals (cash US$220.245m + other financial assets US$228.847m, S3 p.5) used two paragraphs later in the SOTP bridge.
challenges.answer: The paragraph is rewritten to the 30 June 2026 actuals: the FY2025A year-end debt is labelled as such (S0), the half-year stack is given from the LK (short-term bank loans F63 63.228, cash F61 220.245, other financial assets F62 228.847), and the model FY2026E cash is labelled a forecast, not an actual.

challenges.challenge: Three downside facts are softened or missing: (i) S8's headline sanction round runs to licence freezing ('denda hingga pembekuan izin') and further administrative sanctions on market participants 'terkait kasus DSSA dan CUAN' — the report records only the TC Pte Ltd fine; (ii) PTRO's price fragility channel (MSCI/FTSE index-inclusion speculation per the S10 clarification request, 4.85% single-day fall on the rights announcement) is not carried into the mark risk; (iii) the rights issue's 1.66% maximum dilution and the parent's take-up cash call at 46.71% are unquantified although the report calls the issue a catalyst.
challenges.answer: Scope confirmed with S8 quotes: the licence-freeze is an underwriter licence (Wakil Penjamin Emisi Efek) in the DSSA case and the further participant sanctions fall on exchange members and market participants, not on CUAN or its mines (sections 5 and 6). The PTRO-mark risk now carries the exchange volatility letter, the company reply and its MSCI market-evaluation acknowledgement (S10), plus the 4.85% fall on the rights news (F53). The dilution is sized: up to 1.66% for a non-subscriber (F75) on an issue capped at 1.69% of capital (F74), with the parent pro-rata take-up framed against group cash (F61) because the subscription price is undisclosed.

missing_bull_case.note: No upside case is quantified: PTRO's 1H2026 discontinued profit of US$7.620m is excluded from the bubble argument, the >US$1bn order book in the revenue basis has no fact, the S6 coking-coal start and met-coal mix are absent, and no scenario tests the market being right on the PTRO mark.

missing_bear_case.note: Bear side is understated where it counts: S8's headline includes licence-freezing sanctions whose scope for CUAN is unchecked, S10's MSCI/FTSE index-inclusion speculation behind PTRO volatility is unmentioned, and the 1.66% rights-issue dilution plus the quantified parent cash call are not sized.

assumption_realism.note: opex_pct 4.5% bakes in 1H26 other operating income (+US$9.060m incl. a US$42.717m FX gain); tax_rate 10% contradicts its own citation (5.443/14.287 = 38.1%); minority 4.8% ignores the 1H26 attribution; nwc_pct 34.1% triples working capital with no fact.

evidence_and_citations.note: Load-bearing SOTP inputs lack quotes: the US$3.0/t reserve value has no source (S7 gives tonnage only), holdco_net_debt US$641.0 has no fact id or itemised derivation, and the order-book and 1H26-balance-sheet-consistency claims are uncited.

valuation_method_fit.note: Coal block marked on stated reserves conflicts with the stated design (multiple x sourced segment EBITDA or book); report claims an own-history P/E multiple but the engine used peer median; required outputs missing: holdco opex ~10x charge, own 5y discount range, look-through earnings/leverage, upstream coverage, catalyst_date, factor tags.

bias_and_tone.note: Prose leans bearish beyond evidence: PTRO profit quoted as US$1.313m excludes US$7.620m discontinued profit; FY2025A leverage cited at US$131.4m EBITDA excludes depletion/amortisation facts F8/F9; the zero discount still leaves parts far below price, so the call survives — but the per-share figures flatter it.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Deck variables are read correctly: USD-reporting with usd_idr FY2027E 18350 live translation risk flagged, BI rate and coal-realisation basis consistent with ADRO.JK/DSSA.JK conglomerate peers; cost of debt 8.5% coupon-based is the defensible choice over the engine's 6.99% CoC line.

conservatism_audit.note: Stack points one way on history and cash: D&A restatement omits F8/F9 depletion and amortisation (understates FY2025A EBITDA by US$46.0m), nwc jump drains US$357.4m FY2026E cash with no source, while forecast tax 10% and minority 4.8% flatter parent earnings — unsourced in both directions.

calibration.note: All three BLOCK flags carry justifications but two rest on shaky ground: the 11.2pp EBITDA-margin gap is partly an artefact of the incomplete D&A restatement, and extreme_call cites FY2025A EBITDA of US$131.4m against net debt when the full D&A charge implies US$177.4m.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. All FATAL/MATERIAL challenges (C1-C14) are answered on substance: the coal block is re-marked off the typed US$3.00/t reserve multiple to the group reported invested capital (F45, US$381.867m), the SOTP is itemised with the PTRO stake at the sourced market mark, the coal concessions at carrying value and E&E at F44 US$44.332m, and holdco net debt is rebuilt line-by-line - the three Petrosea legs excluded by name, verified by QC at US$652.035m against the notes. SELL, Rp94, TR -81.5% stands on the parts, which even undiscounted sit far below a price the reverse-DCF cannot justify. The 0.30 holdco discount is the middle of the house band and is not rating-moving at a price 3.4x the pre-discount SOTP (CUAN, -81.5%, sits at the bearish end with DSSA -50.1%; the mixed book is parts-based holdcos, not a shared tilt). Two record-hygiene items, neither rating-moving, flagged for the published edition: the C2 response prose still shows the interim US$705.973m holdco figure while the final model carries US$652.035m, and C11 refers to the P/BV weight being cut to 10% while the engine weight renormalises to 16.7% (0.15/0.90); the P/BV leg at Rp64 sits below the SOTP and only lowers the target - conservative for a SELL. Judge returned no verdict this round (output cap), so this sign-off rests on the QC audit (round 3, PASS). No stage change - the Director publishes.

bias.note: Audited both directions. The round-2 BLOCK (Q7) is fixed and verified line by line against the archived filing: S3 note 28 splits the US$109.592m balance-sheet sukuk line into the PARENT Sukuk Wakalah Berkelanjutan I Petrindo Jaya Kreasi (Tahap I 19.602 + Tahap II 36.402 = 56.004, stays in the charge) and Sukuk Ijarah Berkelanjutan I Petrosea (Tahap I 26.154 + Tahap II 28.001 = 54.155, excluded); S3 note 27 splits the bonds into Obligasi Berkelanjutan I Petrindo Jaya Kreasi 112.007 (parent, stays in) and Obligasi Berkelanjutan I Petrosea (Phase I 53.371 + Phase II 56.004 = 109.375, excluded); S3 note 29 lists the syndicated facility split by entity as 'PT Petrosea Tbk 161.862'. The three excluded legs (161.862 + 109.375 + 54.155 = 325.392) are exactly Petrosea's, so holdco net debt 977.427 - 325.392 = 652.035 is right on the report's own stated principle (exclude the listed subsidiary's debt because its equity market mark is already struck after it). The move is traceable to that alone: at 112,418.9m shares, 18115 IDR/USD and the 30% discount, the 53.938m reduction lifts the SOTP leg about Rp6.1 and the blended, COE-capitalised target from Rp88 to Rp94 (about +6%); gross value (Petrosea 46.71% x market cap 2182.119 = 1019.268 + coal F45 381.867 + projects F44 44.332 = 1445.467), the 30% discount, the 83.3/16.7 weights, the P/BV leg (64) and the scenarios (base 94 / bear 78 / bull 110) are undisturbed. Direction of the fix: it REMOVES a ~US$54m (about 6% of target) conservatism, so the SELL is left standing on a higher, more defensible target, not a lower one. The residual asymmetries are disclosed rather than hidden and net roughly opposite: the entity-unattributed bank lines stay in the charge (conservative) while Petrosea's unsplittable cash stays in group cash (generous); neither overturns the -81.5% call, which rests on marking the Petrosea 'bubble' at market — the card's instruction — less the card's discount. No unsupported bullish or bearish step found in a load-bearing number.

The P/E leg is STRUCK, not trimmed: the only trailing metric available is FY2025A parent profit of US$134.567m [S2], and the group's FY2025A profit before tax of US$149.270m [S2/F23] is smaller than its non-cash other operating income of US$193.701m [S2/F20], so normalised ex that item the group was LOSS-MAKING on operations in its last audited year and there is no positive normalised earnings base to capitalise. Capitalising the unadjusted figure at a peer multiple is therefore unsupported optimism, not a corroborating cross-check [S0]. The two remaining legs are re-normalised by the engine to SOTP 83.3% and P/BV 16.7%. SOTP also fits the conglomerate card, which values holdings on their parts first.
